claim: Crb3 knockout mice die shortly after birth

evidence: Supported by citation to Whiteman et al., 2014

claim: The loxP sites flanked either side of exon 3 in the Crb3 gene
source: The loxP sites flanked either side of exon 3 in the Crb3 gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing the construction strategy

claim: Both isoforms Crb3a and Crb3b are knocked out in the mice
source: According to the construction strategy, we are knocking out both isoforms Crb3a and Crb3b in the mice.
evidence: Based on the construction strategy described

claim: Most Crb3fl/fl; CAG-Cre pups died within a few days after birth
source: However, most Crb3fl/fl; CAG-Cre pups died within a few days after birth.

source: Together, these results indicate that Crb3 is necessary for eye development.

claim: Crb3fl/fl; MMTV-Cre mice displayed significantly increased numbers of terminal end buds (TEBs) compared to Crb3fl/fl mice

claim: Crb3 knockout led to ductal epithelial hyperplasia with increased ductal thickness in Crb3fl/fl; MMTV-Cre mice

claim: PyMT-cKO-Crb3 mice developed larger tumors with faster tumor progression and a poorly differentiated phenotype compared to PyMT-WT mice
source: PyMT-WT mice exhibited loss of epithelial features and developed breast cancer, while PyMT-cKO-Crb3 mice developed larger tumors with faster tumor progression and a poorly differentiated phenotype (Figure 1G).

source: Thus, these results suggest that Crb3 knockout leads to ductal epithelial hyperplasia and promotes tumorigenesis.
